title: The Ultimate Guide to Specifying Soundproof Windows
metaTitle: Soundproof Window Buying Guide | Kiran Slido Craft
metaDescription: Everything you need to know about specifying soundproof windows, from STC ratings to frame materials and glazing.
description: Learn the technical factors behind acoustic fenestration, from STC ratings to frame engineering and glass configuration.
excerpt: A deep dive into STC ratings, frame engineering, and glass configurations for maximum noise reduction.

content.text: STC (Sound Transmission Class) is the most critical metric. For high-noise environments near highways or airports, we recommend systems with a minimum STC of 45dB.
The frame is as important as the glass. Our heavy-duty aluminum sections are engineered with multi-chamber profiles to minimize sound resonance.

title: Understanding STC vs. OITC: Which Metric Matters?
metaTitle: STC vs. OITC Explained | Acoustic Performance Metrics
metaDescription: Learn the difference between STC and OITC ratings and how to choose the right one for your noise containment project.
description: A technical comparison of acoustic ratings and how they apply to urban vs. aircraft noise containment.
excerpt: Comparing two critical acoustic metrics and their real-world applications in urban noise containment.

content.text: STC measures speech-range noise. OITC measures low-frequency rumble. If your project is near a construction site or railway, OITC is the metric you should focus on.
Asymmetrical glazing (using two different thicknesses of glass) is the most effective way to block broad-spectrum noise.
